```{r}
a.**What is a genomic range and what 3 types of information do you need for a range?**
A genomic range is a way to display the start or end regions of a given genome.Although the textbook describes it as integer intervals that represent a subsequent of consecutive positions. The three pieces of informations are typically chromosome names, start position, and the end posistion.

b.**What does 0-based and 1-based refer to? What are the advantages and disadvantages of each?**
This refers to two flavors of range systems used to format the ranges -- both coordinate systems -- 0-based is with a half-closed half-open intervals; whereas 1-based is a fully closed intervals in the coordinate system

c.**What is the value of BEDtools over the bioconductor package GenomicRange?**
GenomicRange has a cost associated with loading large sets of data into the memory at once. Whereas using the command line of BEDtools to read the files is faster.
  
d.**Describe one subcommand of the BEDtools suite as well as a practical use case.**

Personally I believe that could be useful. Although it seems somewhat similar (probably not similar at all) to bedtools sort
